name: The Plane Tree of Dobrentei Square

location.address: Dobrentei ter, corner nearest Rudas Gyogyfurdo, Buda bridgehead of Erzsebet hid, Budapest I. kerulet

story: Everything else on this square went. Twentieth-century clearance took Tabán's palaces, its cafes and its Serbian Orthodox church, and the oldest thing left standing on Döbrentei tér is a plane tree of about 115 years. Photographs from the 1900s and 1910s catch it as a young tree, which is how a Budapest history publication dated it, and FŐKERT, the city's parks company, carries it on its own register of notable trees. The trunk is over four metres around and the crown reaches about twenty metres, higher than the roofs beside it, and visibly lopsided, because the tree has never been able to spread toward the building at its back. It came through the fighting around Buda Castle in the 1940s that flattened much of this neighbourhood, and then through the rebuilding of the Elizabeth Bridge, when trees at the bridgehead were candidates for removal. District I gave it local protection in 2011 and fixed a plaque to the trunk. The beer garden at its foot took the name Platán from it, and generations have used the tables in its shade as a meeting point. A second plane stands nearby by the Rudas baths; this entry is the Döbrentei tér tree, the documented and protected one. The pagoda tree at Buda Castle is 350 metres uphill, the Tabán mulberry about 600.
access: Free, standing in a public square
transport: Dobrentei ter tram stop (lines 19/41) or a 5 minute walk from Rudas Gyogyfurdo, on foot

name: The Black Walnut of the Franciscan Ruins

location.address: Margaret Island, Also Nagyret (Lower Great Meadow), beside Arnyas setany, next to the ruins of the Franciscan church and monastery

story: Budapest's biggest black walnut is also the frailest tree on this list, and both facts come from the same survey. FŐKERT, the city's parks company, dated it to around 213 years in its 2020 dendrological study of Margaret Island, which makes it roughly 219 now, and measured its trunk as the thickest black walnut on the island by a wide margin: the runner-up was 119 centimetres smaller around. A national database ranked it second in Hungary for trunk girth. It was probably one of the first trees planted here, in the early 1800s under head gardener Károly Tost, beside the palatine's summer residence. A 1907 newspaper piece describes a walnut in a meadow at the island's centre, 3.5 metres around and 25 metres tall, almost certainly this one. The same 2020 assessment found it hollow and rotting at the trunk and root collar, its crown cut hard back after storm damage and a safety pruning in 2016, and estimated it had about a decade left. That window closes around 2030. It was standing at the last assessment and it is very likely standing now, but the newest evidence here is six years old, so go with your eyes open. It stands by the Franciscan ruins, a hundred metres from the island's oldest yew and 350 from its oldest oak.

best_time.label: late September into October, when the green-husked walnuts drop and stain everything they touch

transport: Margaret Island, roughly 10-12 minute walk north from the Margaret Bridge entrance, or the island's internal bus (26) to the nearest stop

name: The Island's Oldest Pedunculate Oak

location.address: Margaret Island, Felso Rozsakert (Upper Rose Garden), immediately beside Zielinszky Szilard setany

story: This oak is older than the park it stands in. Margaret Island was redeveloped as a landscape park under Archduke Joseph in the 19th century, and a handful of trees on the higher, better-drained eastern strip predate that work as remnants of the oak, ash and elm floodplain forest that covered the ground before anybody designed anything. This pedunculate oak is the island's largest and one of its oldest: FŐKERT's 2020 survey dates it to around 203 years then, so roughly 209 now, and a 1988 measurement put it at 28 to 30 metres tall with a trunk 345 centimetres around. Little of that old forest is left. Around a hundred oaks over ninety years old remain on the island's public land, most of the losses coming from the 2010 flood and the storms of that decade. Its shape records a life spent in a crowd. The crown is asymmetric from growing hemmed in by neighbours, structural limbs were cut back decades ago, and the cavities left by removed branches have recently been treated. Nothing in the record suggests decline, though the most recent condition assessment is the 2020 one. It stands in the Upper Rose Garden beside Zielinszky Szilárd sétány, about 350 metres from the Tree of Science, the Seven Chieftains Plane and the island's black walnut, which together make a loop of under two kilometres.
transport: Margaret Island, roughly 12-15 minute walk north from the Margaret Bridge entrance, near the Rose Garden

name: The Island's Oldest Yew

location.address: Margaret Island, Also Nagyret (Lower Great Meadow), near the ruins of the Franciscan church and monastery

story: Two old yews stand near the Franciscan ruins on Margaret Island, and only one of them still reads as a tree. This is the larger. The other was cut back radically decades ago for reasons nobody wrote down, and now sits at 4.5 metres tall under a crown 7 to 8 metres wide, so anyone comparing the two is not looking at damage from the same event but at one tree that was left alone and one that was not. FŐKERT's 2020 survey of the island calls this the largest and oldest yew there, with nothing comparable anywhere else on the island, and dates it to around 203 years at the time, so roughly 209 now. A former head gardener put it in the 1800s independently. A 1967 survey recorded four old shrub-form yews on the island, two of them standing on their own by the Franciscan ruins; this is one of that pair. For a yew, 209 years is nothing. The species runs to millennia, and English churchyards hold specimens ten times this age, which makes the island's oldest yew a young tree with old damage: rot at the root collar and trunk, bark loss, a major limb long gone leaving the crown truncated, lower branches clipped since a 2012 tidy-up. The most recent assessment is 2020. The black walnut is a hundred metres away.
transport: Margaret Island, roughly 10-12 minute walk north from the Margaret Bridge entrance, near the Franciscan ruins
